title: APT Principles and Agents Distribution Contract

rules: Paths are repository-relative and cannot escape the canonical repository.
Directories expand recursively in deterministic lexical order.
Extensions are acyclic and duplicate entries are invalid.

agentContract.filenameRule: agents/<domain>/<id>.md where <id> is kebab-case and unique across every domain directory

fields.id: Equals the filename without .md. Kebab-case. Unique across all agents/<domain>/ directories. Immutable once published; a rename is a new id plus a deprecation note on the old file.
fields.domain: One canonical domain directory name under agents/.

scope.global: Generator places the adapter at the platform agents root; installs into every repo whose platform list includes the target platform. Core leads, orchestration, and adopted personas.
scope.domain: Generator places the adapter under a domain subdirectory; installs only when a selected manifest pulls the matching agents/<domain> selection.
scope.project: Never auto-installed. A repo opts in by referencing the exact agents/<domain>/<id>.md path in its own manifest.

fields.description: Imperative, one paragraph: WHEN to invoke this agent. Mirrors the body "## When to Use".
fields.persona: Optional reference to an agent persona lens documented in this agent source or a linked source. It is framing guidance only; it is not a product/customer persona, role definition, permission, tool capability, or authority grant.
fields.applies_principles: List of repository-relative principles/**/*.md paths this agent enforces at review time. At least one for agents in an enforceable domain (security-risk, risk, payments, api, architecture, ai, ecommerce, harness). Every path must resolve.
fields.uses_skills: List of repository-relative skills/<domain>/<name> directory paths whose procedure the agent runs. Usually one. Every path must resolve.

tools.meaning: Abstract capability names. scripts/build-agent-adapters.mjs maps these to each platform's real tool identifiers. Default [read, search] for review perspectives.

model_tier.meaning: Capability tier, never a model id. deep for architecture, cross-perspective synthesis, security, and high-stakes reasoning; standard otherwise.

autonomy.meaning: advisory = returns findings only; bounded-edit = may make scoped changes within the task; none = classification or routing only.

fields.escalation: One sentence naming what this agent escalates and to whom. Mirrors the body "## Escalation Rules".
fields.handoffs: Optional JSON-encoded array of routing contracts. Each item has target (existing agent id), when (non-empty trigger), required_evidence (one or more concrete inputs), and expected_output (non-empty deliverable).

rules: "## Perspective-Specific Checks" is required for shared-core agents and must hold at least three checks that change what evidence the agent inspects, which risks it owns, how it evaluates, or when it withholds approval (the agent-authoring-guide ratchet, enforced by npm run validate:specialization).
"## Enforces" is required and must link every principle in applies_principles to the exact canonical principle path, with an actionable check on the same bullet.
Optional handoffs must be JSON-encoded frontmatter arrays; each target must resolve to a canonical agent id and every item must state a trigger, required evidence, and expected output.
The body is written in second person so it also serves as the platform system prompt.

The canonical agents/<domain>/<id>.md file is the single source. platforms/<platform>/source/agents/** is generated by scripts/build-agent-adapters.mjs and must be reproducible from canonical; hand edits are drift.
Every applies_principles and uses_skills path must resolve.
New agents and agent renames must pass npm run validate:agents and npm run validate:specialization.
Generated adapter targets and capabilities are defined by references/agent-platform-capabilities.json.
The target owns and commits the installation record.
Managed files record canonical source, target path, artifact kind, and installed SHA-256.
Sync preserves local drift unless force is explicit.
Forced replacement writes a local timestamped backup before overwrite.
Applied operations refresh source version, commit, hashes, and last operation.
